title: Ring and module transport through the localized nerve
statement: For small sites C,J and E,K, let R and A be commutative coefficient ring sheaves and F:E→Sh(J). Suppose N:Sh(J)≃Sh(K) has underlying Hom nerve of F, and g is a ringed equivalence from (K,A) to (J,R) whose inverse image equals N.functor and whose structural map is invertible. Fix whole module comparison data [def-sp-binary-presentation-module-data]. For Z∈E fix a category-of-elements slice equivalence and a slice equivalence Over(FZ)≃Sh(K.over Z) with the Hom nerve formula. There exists a ringed morphism from the fixed localized ring A.over Z to R restricted on the element site of FZ, whose inverse image is exactly the composite of those supplied equivalences, with invertible structural map and exact module comparison data. The whole module equivalence commutes with restriction to Z by an invertible square. The restricted ring is exactly A.over Z, not an independently transported ring.

source.place: Tags 00Y1, 04GZ and 03EH; sites-modules.tex Tags 03CR and 04IE. Auxiliary extraction of the corresponding steps of lem-sp-binary-cover-site-presentation.

proof.text: The Hom nerve and the product universal property give N(M)|Z≅S(FZ×M→FZ). Combine with the supplied element-site fibre equivalence to obtain q:g.inverse⋙K.overPullback Z≅elementSheafPullback(FZ)⋙H.functor. All maps are explicit lifts and projections; prove naturality using the two product projections.

Set the slice inverse and direct images to H.functor and H.inverse. Its structural map is q.inv evaluated at R, followed by restriction of g.ringMap. Naturality for the zero and one maps proves their identities. For addition and multiplication, conjugate their binary-operation equations by q using product preservation, then evaluate on generalized elements. Thus this is real ring data and its structural map is invertible.

Construct the induced module direct image using [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-induced-modules]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-equivalence-module-hom] to get its inverse module equivalence, underlying isomorphism and rank-one equation. Equivalences preserve finite limits/colimits and are additive. Their termwise action gives the ordinary derived equivalence. The linear module-square construction from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-equivalence-slices], with q and its structural equation, gives the restriction square. Compare explicit precomposition with the actual identity-scalar pushforwards.

theorem exists_binaryPresentationRingedSlice
    {C E : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [SmallCategory E]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology E}
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (ring : Sheaf K CommRingCat.{u})
    (F : E ⥤ Sheaf J (Type u)) (N : Sheaf J (Type u) ≌ Sheaf K (Type u))
    (hN : N.functor ⋙ sheafToPresheaf K (Type u) ≅ sheafSubcategoryNerve F)
    (g : RingedToposMorphism (localCoefficientRings ring) (localCoefficientRings R))
    (hi : g.inverse = N.functor) (hr : IsIso g.ringMap)
    (whole : BinaryPresentationModules g)
    (Z : E) (source : RingedSheafSliceAdjunctionData (localCoefficientRings R) (F.obj Z))
    (S : Over (F.obj Z) ≌ Sheaf (K.over Z) (Type u))
    (hS : S.functor ⋙ sheafToPresheaf (K.over Z) (Type u) ≅
      yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringLeft (Over Z)ᵒᵖ
        (Over (F.obj Z))ᵒᵖ (Type u)).obj (Over.post F).op) :
    ∃ e : RingedToposMorphism (localCoefficientRings (ring.over Z))
        (localCoefficientRings (presentationElementRing R (F.obj Z))),
      e.inverse = source.fibreEquivalence.functor ⋙ S.functor ∧
      IsIso e.ringMap ∧
      ∃ loc : BinaryPresentationModules e,
      Nonempty (elementModulePullback (localCoefficientRings R) (F.obj Z) ⋙
          loc.modules.functor ≅
          whole.modules.functor ⋙ SheafOfModules.overFunctor (localCoefficientRings ring) Z)
